description.description: Free-form description rendered in the dialog body (above the form fields, or alongside the confirm prompt). Plain text; line breaks preserved. Available on all kinds.

dialog.description: Dialog presentation overrides (title, size, button labels, confirm style). All fields optional; defaults documented on [`DialogSpec`]. Used by every kind.

form.description: Form field declarations for `kind: form`. Either explicit `fields:` entries or a `table:` reference (or both — explicit entries override the table column's defaults). Ignored by `kind: confirm` and `kind: http_request`.

http.description: HTTP body for `kind: http_request`. Mandatory when the kind is `http_request`; ignored otherwise. Validated at catalog time.

params.description: Positional parameter declarations for `kind: http_request`. Declaration order is the **public contract**: the Rhai host fn `actions.<name>(...)` takes its arguments in this exact order. Ignored by `kind: form` and `kind: confirm` (those use `form:` instead).

stream.description: Command + line filter for `kind: stream`. Mandatory when the kind is `stream`; ignored otherwise. Validated at catalog time.

terminal.description: Command to run for `kind: terminal`. Mandatory when the kind is `terminal`; ignored otherwise. Validated at catalog time.

oneOf.description: Opens a dialog with form fields; returns a record of user input.
Opens a yes/no dialog; returns a bool.
Opens a read-only dialog over resolved `params:`, fires HTTP on confirm. Deliberately narrow — not a form.
Opens a dialog with a description, the command, and a read-only terminal that streams the command's PTY output on Run.
Opens a bottom sheet that runs the command immediately with piped output, filters each line through a Rhai closure, and streams it into a read-only terminal. Killed on close. For live log tails.

Opens a two-column dialog: a `form:` on the left and a read-only terminal on the right. On submit the form disables and the `terminal.command` runs in a PTY with `${form.<field>}` and `${row.<field>}` interpolated, streaming output into the terminal. Requires both `form:` and `terminal:`. Returns unit. Built for "collect inputs, then run a create/apply command".
Integer byte count, rendered as `1.5 KB` / `29.0 MB` / `1.4 GB` (base-1024). Sources that emit a JSON number or a numeric string both work.

DialogSpec.description:
Presentation overrides for the action dialog. All fields optional; the defaults below produce a sensible dialog for any kind.

`title` and `description` support `${row.x}` interpolation at dispatch time when the action is invoked from a row context — see `vantage-actions` runtime for the substitution rules.

confirm_style.description: Visual emphasis of the confirm button. `danger` renders red — reserve for destructive actions (delete, cancel order).

description.description: Free-form body text rendered above the form fields / confirm prompt. Plain text; line breaks preserved.

title.description: Dialog header. Default: humanised action key (`cancel_order` → `"Cancel order"`).

FieldEntry.description: Sugar: a `fields:` entry is either a bare column name (string) OR a full field-def map. Bare strings only make sense when `form.table:` is set — enforced by `catalog::validate`.

choices.description: Enum-style dropdown values. Inherited from the table column when `form.table:` is set and the column declares choices.

default.description: Default value rendered when the dialog opens (and the field is not prefilled from a row). String form — coerced to the field type at render time.

multiline.description: Render a multi-line text area (string fields only).

option_label.description: Column in each `options` row to display. Defaults to the value.

option_value.description: Column in each `options` row to submit as the field value. Defaults to `id`; set it when the option table's id column has a different name (e.g. versions keyed by `version`).

options.description: Rhai *query* script (same surface as a table `cmd:` — `table(..)`, `get_ref(..)`, `add_order(..)`, `list()`) returning the dropdown's option rows. `${row.x}` is interpolated against the action's row before the script runs, so options can be narrowed by the parent record (e.g. a product's versions via `get_ref`). An alternative to a `references:` column as the dropdown's source; the first row returned becomes the default selection.

readonly.description: Render the field disabled (non-editable). Useful for an auto-filled identifier shown for context — e.g. a product id defaulted from `${row.id}` that the user shouldn't change.

type.description: Optional when `form.table:` is set AND the named column resolves there. Required otherwise.

widget.description: Optional renderer override. Today only `dropdown` is wired — it pairs with a `references:` column to surface a select populated from the referenced table's rows. Plain text input is the default when omitted.

FormSpec.description: Form definition for `kind: form` actions. Fields are either declared explicitly or inherited from a referenced table.

fields.description: Field list. Omit when `table:` is set to default to "all writable columns of the table in declaration order".

table.description: When set, fields inherit column metadata (type, label, choices, default) from this table's definition. Bare-string entries in `fields:` resolve against this table. Validated in `catalog::validate` to require this when any shorthand entry is present.

oneOf.description: Render a select populated from the referenced table's rows. Only valid on a column that declares `references:`; otherwise `catalog::validate` flags the field.

HttpSpec.description: HTTP execution body for `kind: http_request`. URL and header values support `${ENV_VAR}` substitution from the process environment at call time (unset = catalog warning + action disabled). JSON body values are Rhai expressions evaluated with the resolved param map in scope — bare names reference params (`body.email: email`).

body.description: Flat key→value JSON body. Values are Rhai expressions; for a literal string write `"'literal'"`. Nested objects are not supported in v1 — flatten or stringify upstream.

label.description: Human label rendered in the read-only confirmation dialog's parameter table. `None` falls back to a humanised form of the param name (`client_id` → `Client id`).

required.description: Required at call time. Defaults to `true`. Optional params land when arity-overloading is wired in a follow-up.

type.description: Static type. Used for type-checking the arguments passed in the row-action Rhai body when the host fn is registered.

StreamSpec.description:
The command a `kind: stream` action runs. Unlike `kind: terminal`, the child is launched with its stdout/stderr **piped** (not a PTY), so a long-running producer like `aws logs tail … --follow` emits clean, uncoloured, line-delimited text — the right input for a per-line Rhai filter. The command runs the instant the sheet opens and is killed when it closes; it receives no input.

`${row.x}` references in `command`/`args`/`cwd` are substituted from the row passed to `actions.<name>(row)` (a row-action body), so a single action can tail whichever stream the user selected.

args.description: Arguments passed to the program, in order. `${row.x}` substituted.

command.description: Program to execute. Resolved on `PATH` or given absolutely.

cwd.description: Working directory for the child. Relative paths resolve against the vista (catalog) root; absent means the vista root itself.

filter.description: Rhai source evaluated **once** to a closure `|line| { … }` that is then called for each output line. The return value decides output: a string is emitted as-is, a map `#{ message, level }` is rendered through the timestamp/level filter, and `()`/`false` drops the line. Absent ⇒ each raw line is emitted verbatim.

TerminalSpec.description: The command a `kind: terminal` action runs. Launched in a PTY (so it believes it is attached to a real TTY — colours, progress bars, line redraws all work) with its output streamed into a read-only terminal. It receives no user input.

args.description: Arguments passed to the program, in order.

command.description: Program to execute. Resolved on `PATH` or given absolutely (e.g. `python3`, `/usr/bin/env`).

cwd.description: Working directory for the child. Relative paths resolve against the vista (catalog) root; absent means the vista root itself.
